records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֛ה בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינַ֖י בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד בְּאֶחָד֩ לַחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֜י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית לְצֵאתָ֛ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses in [the] wilderness of Sinai in [the] tent of meeting on [day] one of the month the second, in the year the second of their going out from [the] land of Egypt, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month in the second year after the people of Israel came out of the land of Egypt. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first [day] of the second month, in the second year of their going out from the land of Egypt, saying,

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the meeting tent in the Desert of Sinai. It was the first day of the second month in the second year after the people of Israel left Egypt. He said,

decisions.choice: the second year after the exodus, in the wilderness of Sinai: the book begins where Exodus and Leviticus leave Israel
decisions.reason: Israel reached the wilderness of Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exodus 19:1), and the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year (Exodus 40:17). Since then the LORD has spoken to Moses from the tent of meeting (Leviticus 1:1). One month later he orders this count of the men who can fight, to prepare the people for the march. They leave Sinai on the twentieth day of this same month (10:11), and the book follows them through the wilderness to the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho (22:1; 36:13).

decisions.choice: wilderness: dry, thinly settled country, used for grazing
decisions.reason: The word names land with too little rain for farming, where flocks could still be grazed (Exodus 3:1). It is not only sand desert. The Hebrew name of the book, "In the wilderness", comes from this verse.

decisions.choice: in the tent of meeting: the LORD now speaks from the tabernacle
decisions.reason: At Sinai God first spoke from the mountain (Exodus 19-20). Once the tent was set up, he met Moses there, speaking from above the ark (Exodus 25:22; 40:34-35; Numbers 7:89).

decisions.choice: after the people of Israel came out / left
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "their going out", meaning Israel's. Balanced and Readable name the people so the date is clear.

records.heading: A census of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai

records.source: שְׂא֗וּ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֙ כָּל־עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם בְּמִסְפַּ֣ר שֵׁמ֔וֹת כָּל־זָכָ֖ר לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Lift up [the] head of all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel by their clans, by [the] house of their fathers, by [the] number of names, every male by their skulls.
pieces: "Take a census of the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} by clans and by ancestral families, listing the names of every male one by one.

L.2: "Lift up the head of all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel by their clans, by the house of their fathers, by the number of names, every male by their heads.

R.2: "Count the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} by clans and families. List every male by name, one by one.

decisions.choice: lift up the head: take a census, count
decisions.reason: To "lift up the head" of a group is to count it (Exodus 30:12). The same phrase returns in verse 49 and 26:2. The command is plural: it is addressed to Moses and Aaron together (verse 3).

decisions.choice: clans and the house of their fathers: the divisions within each tribe
decisions.reason: Israel was made up of tribes, each tribe of clans, and each clan of "fathers' houses", large families named after a common forefather. Joshua 7:14-18 goes down the same steps: tribe, clan, household, man. The census was taken through these family groups.

decisions.choice: by their skulls: one by one, head by head
decisions.reason: The word means "skull". "By the skull" is the way of saying "per head" (Exodus 16:16; 38:26): every male was counted one at a time, by name.

decisions.choice: ancestral families / families
decisions.reason: "House of their fathers" means a family group named after its forefather. Balanced says "ancestral families" and Readable "families"; Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

records.source: מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה כָּל־יֹצֵ֥א צָבָ֖א בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל תִּפְקְד֥וּ אֹתָ֛ם לְצִבְאֹתָ֖ם אַתָּ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃
records.gloss: From a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army in Israel, you will enroll them by their armies, you and Aaron.
pieces: You and Aaron are to enroll them by their divisions, all the men in Israel twenty years old and up, everyone who can go out to war.

L.3: From a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army in Israel, you will enroll them by their armies, you and Aaron.

R.3: You and Aaron must count every man in Israel who is twenty years old or older and can go out to war. List them by their troops.

decisions.choice: every one going out to the army: every man fit for military service
decisions.reason: The word translated "army" means a host or a body of men on service, most often in war. "Going out" is the regular verb for marching out to battle (Deuteronomy 20:1). The count is of men able to fight, from the age of twenty up (Exodus 30:14; 38:26).

decisions.choice: enroll: count and register for service
decisions.reason: The verb means to look after, to take note of, and so to muster or enroll men for a task. It is the key verb of the chapter (verses 19, 44) and is used again in verse 50 in the sense "appoint".

decisions.choice: by their armies: by their military divisions
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for army here means the companies or divisions into which the men were grouped, as in 2:3-31, where each tribe camps "by its armies".

decisions.choice: You and Aaron are to enroll them ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "you and Aaron" at the end for emphasis. Balanced and Readable name them first, as English does, and put the age and the purpose after.

decisions.choice: all the men / every man; divisions / troops
decisions.reason: Those counted are the males of verse 2, so Balanced and Readable say "men". The army units are "armies" at Literal, "divisions" at Balanced and "troops" at Readable, here and through the book.

records.source: וְאִתְּכֶ֣ם יִהְי֔וּ אִ֥ישׁ אִ֖ישׁ לַמַּטֶּ֑ה אִ֛ישׁ רֹ֥אשׁ לְבֵית־אֲבֹתָ֖יו הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And with you will be a man, a man for the tribe; a man [who is] head of [the] house of his fathers [is] he.
pieces: One man from each tribe is to be with you, each of them the head of his ancestral family.

L.4: And with you there will be a man, a man for [each] tribe, a man who [is] head of the house of his fathers.

R.4: One man from each tribe will work with you. Each one will be the leader of his family group.

decisions.choice: a man, a man for the tribe: one man from each tribe
decisions.reason: Saying a word twice gives it a distributive sense in Hebrew: "a man, a man" means "one man each". Verse 44 counts them: twelve men.

decisions.choice: head of the house of his fathers: a family head who also leads his tribe
decisions.reason: Each helper was the head of a leading family in his tribe. Verse 16 calls the same men leaders of their tribes, and they lead their tribes again in 2:3-31, 7:12-83 and 10:14-27.

decisions.choice: will work with you
decisions.reason: "Be with you" here means to help with the count (verse 5, "stand with you"). Readable says so.

records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ שְׁמ֣וֹת הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַֽעַמְד֖וּ אִתְּכֶ֑ם לִרְאוּבֵ֕ן אֱלִיצ֖וּר בֶּן־שְׁדֵיאֽוּר׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] names of the men who will stand with you: for Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
pieces: These are the names of the men who are to assist you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur,

L.5: And these [are] the names of the men who will stand with you: for Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur,

R.5: Here are the names of the men who will help you: From Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur.

decisions.choice: stand with you: assist you, serve beside you
decisions.reason: To "stand with" someone is to support or help them. The twelve men are not counted themselves as a separate group; they help Moses and Aaron carry out the count.

decisions.choice: the order of the tribes: by the mothers of Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: The list in verses 5-15 starts with the sons of Leah (Reuben, Simeon, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun), then the sons of Rachel (Joseph, counted as Ephraim and Manasseh, and Benjamin), then the sons of the servant women Bilhah and Zilpah (Dan, Asher, Gad, Naphtali) (Genesis 35:23-26). Levi is left out (verses 47-49).

decisions.choice: Elizur, Shedeur: names that speak of God
decisions.reason: Several leaders' names are formed with a word for God: El ("God"), Shaddai ("the Almighty") or Zur ("rock"). Elizur probably means "my God is a rock". The same names return in 2:10, 7:30 and 10:18.

decisions.reason: He leads Simeon again in 2:12, 7:36 and 10:19. Zurishaddai means "my rock is the Almighty"; Shelumiel probably "God is my peace".

pieces: from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab,

decisions.choice: Nahshon son of Amminadab: Aaron's brother-in-law, an ancestor of David
decisions.reason: Aaron married Nahshon's sister Elisheba (Exodus 6:23), and Nahshon's line leads to David (Ruth 4:20-22). Judah's camp goes first in 2:3 and 10:14, and Nahshon brings the first offering in 7:12.

decisions.reason: He leads Issachar again in 2:5, 7:18 and 10:15. Nethanel means "God has given".

decisions.reason: He leads Zebulun again in 2:7, 7:24 and 10:16. He is a different man from Eliab the Reubenite, the father of Dathan and Abiram (16:1).

pieces: from the descendants of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,

L.10: for the sons of Joseph: for Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; for Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,

R.10: From Joseph's descendants: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

decisions.choice: the sons of Joseph: Ephraim and Manasseh count as two tribes
decisions.reason: Jacob adopted Joseph's two sons as his own (Genesis 48:5), so Joseph's descendants form two tribes. With Levi set apart (verses 47-49), that keeps the number of tribes at twelve.

decisions.choice: Elishama son of Ammihud: a forefather of Joshua
decisions.reason: In 1 Chronicles 7:26-27 Elishama son of Ammihud is in the line of Ephraim that leads to Joshua son of Nun.

decisions.choice: Abidan son of Gideoni: the leader of Benjamin
decisions.reason: He leads Benjamin again in 2:22, 7:60 and 10:24. Abidan means "my father is judge", a name for God as father.

decisions.reason: He leads Dan again in 2:25, 7:66 and 10:25. Ahiezer means "my brother is help"; Ammishaddai, like Zurishaddai (verse 6), contains the divine name Shaddai, "the Almighty".

decisions.reason: He leads Asher again in 2:27, 7:72 and 10:26.

pieces: from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel,

L.14: for Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel,

R.14: From Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.

decisions.choice: Deuel: the spelling of the Hebrew text here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text spells his father's name Deuel here and in 7:42, 47 and 10:20, but Reuel in 2:14. In Hebrew writing the letters d and r look very much alike, and one spelling probably arose from the other. It is the same man either way.

R.15: From Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."

decisions.choice: Ahira son of Enan: the leader of Naphtali
decisions.reason: He leads Naphtali again in 2:29, 7:78 and 10:27. Naphtali, the last of the sons of the servant women, closes the list, as it closes the camps in 2:29-31.

records.source: אֵ֚לֶּה קְרוּאֵ֣י הָעֵדָ֔ה נְשִׂיאֵ֖י מַטּ֣וֹת אֲבוֹתָ֑ם רָאשֵׁ֛י אַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽם׃
records.gloss: These [were the] called [ones] of the congregation, leaders of [the] tribes of their fathers; heads of [the] thousands of Israel [were] they.
pieces: These were the men chosen from the congregation, the leaders of their ancestral tribes. They were the heads of the clans of Israel.

L.16: These [were] the called [ones] of the congregation, the leaders of the tribes of their fathers; they [were] the heads of the thousands of Israel.

R.16: These men were chosen from the community. They were the leaders of their tribes and the heads of Israel's clans.

decisions.choice: the called ones: the marginal reading
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew spells this word in a slightly different way; the Masoretes' marginal reading gives the usual form of "called ones". The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the called ones of the congregation: men summoned to act for the people
decisions.reason: They are chosen representatives, called by name (verse 17). Similar titles are given to the leaders who rise up with Korah (16:2) and to Dathan and Abiram (26:9).

decisions.choice: the thousands of Israel: the large family groups within the tribes
decisions.reason: The word usually means "thousand", but it can also name a unit within a tribe, a clan or division. Gideon says "my thousand is the weakest in Manasseh" (Judges 6:15), and Israel stands before the LORD "by your tribes and by your thousands" (1 Samuel 10:19). Here it stands beside "tribes" and names the groups these men led. On the word in the census totals, see the note at verse 21.

decisions.choice: clans
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "thousands" are here, divisions of a tribe. "Clans" gives that sense, though it is not the word for "clans" used in verse 2. Literal keeps "thousands".

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִקְּב֖וּ בְּשֵׁמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And took Moses and Aaron the men the these who were designated by names.
pieces: Moses and Aaron took these men who had been named,

L.17: And Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by names.

R.17: Moses and Aaron brought together these men who had been chosen by name.

decisions.choice: designated by names: singled out by name
decisions.reason: The verb means to mark out or specify. The men were not volunteers; each was named for the task (verses 5-15). The same expression is used of men chosen for a task in 1 Chronicles 12:32 and Ezra 8:20.

decisions.choice: took these men ... , and they gathered
decisions.reason: Balanced joins this verse to the next with a comma, since the gathering of the people in verse 18 follows directly on Moses and Aaron taking the twelve men.

records.source: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־הָעֵדָ֜ה הִקְהִ֗ילוּ בְּאֶחָד֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וַיִּתְיַֽלְד֥וּ עַל־מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם בְּמִסְפַּ֣ר שֵׁמ֗וֹת מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֛ה וָמַ֖עְלָה לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And all the congregation they assembled on [day] one of the month the second, and they declared their descent by their clans, by [the] house of their fathers, by [the] number of names, from a son of twenty years and upward, by their skulls,
pieces: and they gathered the whole congregation on the first day of the second month. The people registered their descent by clans and ancestral families, and the names of those twenty years old and up were listed one by one,

L.18: And they assembled all the congregation on the first [day] of the second month, and they declared their descent by their clans, by the house of their fathers, by the number of names, from a son of twenty years and upward, by their heads,

R.18: On the first day of the second month they called the whole community together. The people were listed by their clans and families. Every man twenty years old or older was counted by name, one by one.

decisions.choice: declared their descent: had their family line recorded
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root "to bear a child" and is used only here, in a form that means each person had himself listed by descent. Each man was entered under his clan and family.

decisions.choice: on the first day of the second month: the same day the command was given
decisions.reason: Verse 1 gives the same date. The people were gathered at once, on the day the LORD spoke.

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they". Balanced and Readable make clear that the people, not Moses and Aaron, had their descent recorded.

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַֽיִּפְקְדֵ֖ם בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃פ
records.gloss: Just as had commanded Yahweh Moses, and he enrolled them in [the] wilderness of Sinai.
pieces: just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses. So Moses enrolled them in the wilderness of Sinai.

L.19: just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses. And he enrolled them in the wilderness of Sinai.

R.19: Moses did this just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him. He counted them in the Desert of Sinai.

decisions.choice: just as the LORD had commanded Moses: the count was done as ordered
decisions.reason: The phrase looks back to the command of verses 2-3. The same note of obedience closes the chapter (verse 54) and runs through the building of the tabernacle (Exodus 39:1-43).

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he enrolled them". Balanced and Readable name Moses, the "he" of the sentence.

records.gloss: And were [the] sons of Reuben, [the] firstborn of Israel, their generations, by their clans, by [the] house of their fathers, by [the] number of names, by their skulls, every male from a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army,
pieces: The descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every male twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name, one by one.

decisions.choice: forty-six thousand five hundred: the word read as the number "thousand"
alternatives: forty-six units (clans or military companies) with five hundred men in all
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary Hebrew word for "thousand", and the text treats these figures as numbers: the twelve totals add up exactly to 603,550 (verse 46), the same figure as the count of men who paid the half shekel (Exodus 38:26), and close to the "about 600,000 men on foot" who left Egypt (Exodus 12:37). The firstborn sons are counted at 22,273 (3:43), which also fits a very large people. But more than 600,000 fighting men implies a whole people of perhaps two million or more in the wilderness, and that is hard to square with other passages, where Israel is smaller than the nations of Canaan (Deuteronomy 7:7) and too few to fill the land at once (Exodus 23:29-30). The same word can name a unit of a tribe, a clan or a military company (verse 16; Judges 6:15; 1 Samuel 10:19). Read that way, Reuben's figure would be forty-six units with five hundred men in all, and the totals would be far smaller. That reading has to treat the sums in verse 46 and 2:32 as a later misunderstanding, so the text as it stands is followed here, and the question is left open.

decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "enroll" (verse 3) and means those who were mustered. Each tribe's total is given in the same words in verses 21-43.

decisions.choice: 603,550: the same total as in Exodus
decisions.reason: The twelve tribal totals add up to exactly this number. It is the same as the number of men who paid the half shekel when the tabernacle was built (Exodus 38:26), and it is repeated when the camps are arranged (2:32). The second census, near the end of the wilderness years, gives 601,730 (26:51). On the size of these numbers, see the note at verse 21.
The Hebrew writes "six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty". All three levels give it in figures.

decisions.choice: the Levites were not enrolled: their count comes later, and in a different way
decisions.reason: Levi is counted separately in chapter 3, every male from one month old (3:15, 39), and again for the work of carrying the tabernacle, from thirty to fifty (4:2-3, 46-48). They were not counted for war, because their service was at the tabernacle (verses 50-53).

decisions.choice: were not enrolled: a rare passive form
decisions.reason: The verb "enroll" appears here in an unusual passive form that is found only a few times. The sense is plain: they were not entered in this count.

decisions.choice: with the other tribes
decisions.reason: "Among them" means among the tribes just counted. Readable says so.

decisions.choice: For / This was because
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the link to verse 47 clear (m1).

decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: The one tribe you are not to enroll is Levi.
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "the tribe of Levi" first for emphasis. Balanced keeps the emphasis with "the one tribe".

records.gloss: And you, appoint the Levites over [the] tabernacle of the testimony and over all its vessels and over all that [belongs] to it; they will carry the tabernacle and all its vessels, and they will serve it, and around the tabernacle they will camp.
pieces: Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the testimony, all its furnishings and everything that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, look after it, and camp around the tabernacle.

L.50: But you, appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, and over all its furnishings, and over all that [belongs] to it. They will carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, and they will serve it, and around the tabernacle they will camp.

R.50: Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle, the tent where the covenant tablets are kept. They are in charge of all its equipment and everything that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and its equipment. They must take care of it and set up their tents all around it.

decisions.choice: appoint: the same verb as "enroll", used in another sense
decisions.reason: The verb that means "enroll" in verse 49 means "appoint" or "put in charge" here. Moses is not to enroll the Levites for war; he is to appoint them over the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle of the testimony: the tent that held the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: The testimony is the two tablets of the covenant kept in the ark (Exodus 25:16, 21). The tabernacle is named after them here and in verse 53 (Exodus 38:21).

decisions.choice: serve it: do the work of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the service done at the sanctuary, by priests and by Levites. For the Levites it means looking after the tent and its furnishings and carrying them (3:6-8; 4:4-33).

decisions.choice: the tent where the covenant tablets are kept
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the testimony", as in Exodus 38:21.

decisions.choice: furnishings / equipment
decisions.reason: The word means vessels, utensils or equipment of any kind: here the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars and their tools (3:31; 4:5-15).

records.source: וּבִנְסֹ֣עַ הַמִּשְׁכָּ֗ן יוֹרִ֤ידוּ אֹתוֹ֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם וּבַחֲנֹת֙ הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן יָקִ֥ימוּ אֹת֖וֹ הַלְוִיִּ֑ם וְהַזָּ֥ר הַקָּרֵ֖ב יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And when sets out the tabernacle, will take it down the Levites, and when camps the tabernacle, will set it up the Levites; and the outsider who comes near will be put to death.
pieces: Whenever the tabernacle is to move on, the Levites are to take it down, and whenever it is to be pitched, the Levites are to set it up. Any outsider who comes near it is to be put to death.

L.51: And when the tabernacle sets out, the Levites will take it down, and when the tabernacle camps, the Levites will set it up; and the outsider who comes near will be put to death.

R.51: When it is time to move the tabernacle, the Levites must take it down. When it is time to set it up again, the Levites must do it. Anyone else who comes near it must be put to death.

decisions.choice: the outsider: anyone who is not a Levite
decisions.reason: The word means someone who does not belong to the group in question, not necessarily a foreigner. Here it is any Israelite outside the tribe of Levi; elsewhere it means anyone who is not a priest (3:10; 18:7).

decisions.choice: will be put to death: the penalty set by the law
decisions.reason: The passive form is the usual wording for the death penalty in the law (Exodus 19:12; 21:12). It guards the holy things from careless approach; 4:15, 20 warn that even Levites will die if they touch or look at them wrongly.

decisions.choice: sets out ... camps: the words used of the whole camp on the march
decisions.reason: The tabernacle "sets out" and "camps" with the people. The same two verbs describe Israel's moves throughout the wilderness journey (9:17-23; 10:12; 33:1-49).

decisions.choice: Anyone else
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the outsider is here: anyone who is not a Levite (m1).

records.source: וְחָנ֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֧ישׁ עַֽל־מַחֲנֵ֛הוּ וְאִ֥ישׁ עַל־דִּגְל֖וֹ לְצִבְאֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And will camp [the] sons of Israel, a man by his camp and a man by his standard, by their armies.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are to camp by their divisions, {{gender:everyone|each man}} in {{gender:their|his}} own camp and under {{gender:their|his}} own standard.

L.52: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel will camp, {{gender:each one|each man}} by {{gender:their|his}} camp and {{gender:each one|each man}} by {{gender:their|his}} standard, by their armies.

R.52: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must camp by their troops, {{gender:everyone|each man}} in {{gender:their|his}} own camp and under {{gender:their|his}} own flag.

decisions.choice: standard: the banner of a group in the camp
decisions.reason: The word means a flag or banner that marks a group. In chapter 2 the tribes camp in four groups of three around the tabernacle, each group under one standard (2:2-31).

decisions.choice: a man ... a man: each one
decisions.reason: "A man" repeated means "each". The whole people camps this way, households and all, not only the men just counted.

decisions.choice: each one / everyone, with "each man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Since the whole people is meant (m2), the inclusive wording is the default and the traditional "each man" the alternative.

records.source: וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם יַחֲנ֤וּ סָבִיב֙ לְמִשְׁכַּ֣ן הָעֵדֻ֔ת וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה קֶ֔צֶף עַל־עֲדַ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשָׁמְרוּ֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת מִשְׁכַּ֥ן הָעֵדֽוּת׃
records.gloss: And the Levites will camp around [the] tabernacle of the testimony, and not will be wrath on [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel; and will keep the Levites [the] charge of [the] tabernacle of the testimony.
pieces: But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that no wrath falls on the congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. The Levites are to keep guard over the tabernacle of the testimony."

L.53: And the Levites will camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that there will be no wrath on the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; and the Levites will keep the charge of the tabernacle of the testimony."

R.53: But the Levites must camp all around the tabernacle, so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger does not strike the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. The Levites must guard the tabernacle and take care of it."

decisions.choice: wrath: God's anger when what is holy is treated carelessly
decisions.reason: The word is used of the LORD's anger breaking out against the people when the holy place is wrongly approached (17:11; 18:5; Leviticus 10:6). The Levites' camp around the tent is a guard that protects the people from coming too near.

decisions.choice: keep the charge: stand guard and carry out the duties
decisions.reason: The word means a watch or duty to be kept. For the Levites it is both guarding the tent against intruders and doing its work (3:7-8, 38; 18:3-5).

decisions.choice: my anger
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "there will be no wrath". The LORD is speaking, and the wrath is his (m1), so Readable says "my anger".

decisions.choice: guard the tabernacle and take care of it
decisions.reason: Readable gives both sides of the word "charge" (m2).

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And did [the] sons of Israel according to all that commanded Yahweh Moses; so they did.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses. That is exactly what they did.

L.54: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses; so they did.

R.54: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did exactly what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: they did ... so they did: complete obedience
decisions.reason: Saying "they did" at the start and "so they did" at the end stresses that the people did all they were told, as when the tabernacle was finished (Exodus 39:32, 42-43; 40:16).

decisions.choice: exactly
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the repeated "so they did" with "exactly" instead of repeating the verb.
